key_insight: MultiGP performs generative inverse rendering from a single image by jointly sampling reflectance, texture, and illumination, and resolves radiometric ambiguity by using the fact that all objects in a scene share the same illumination.
problem_solved: Disentangling object-specific reflectance and texture from scene-wide illumination using only a single photograph, where many plausible explanations exist for observed appearance.
method: Probabilistic generative inverse-rendering framework that stochastically samples radiometric constituents (reflectance, texture, illumination) consistent with the image.
Enforces a multi-object consensus constraint: objects with differing materials share a single scene illumination estimate to disambiguate reflectance vs. lighting.
Uses differentiable rendering and posterior sampling to produce multiple plausible decompositions and quantify uncertainty in material and lighting estimates.
impact: Provides a practical way to recover materials and lighting (with uncertainty) from single images, enabling better relighting, material editing, AR insertion, and training data generation for vision and graphics applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: single input image -> probabilistic sampler -> outputs: reflectance maps, textures, and shared illumination map.
Before/after comparisons: original photo vs. separated reflectance, texture layers, and reconstructed relit variants.
Illustration of the multi-object consensus: multiple objects under one inferred illumination vs. independent ambiguous solutions.
Gallery of stochastic samples showing different plausible decompositions and an uncertainty heatmap.
paper_title: Under One Sun: Multi-Object Generative Perception of Materials and Illumination
paper_authors: Nobuo Yoshii, Xinran Nicole Han, Ryo Kawahara, Todd Zickler, Ko Nishino
